pureftpd (24 rows, adjudicated directly): 6 TP (genuine read-only accessors), 18 FP. Notably this INVERTS the task's own stated expectation of a high TP rate for this project -- flagging that reversal explicitly rather than silently deviating. The 18 FP break down as: writes through a derived alias/cursor (freestructs' hash0, generic_parser's config_keywords_pnt, strip_lf's strchr-derived f), a parameter aliased into a global that gets mutated in a different function (clearargs' argv -> argv0, later written by setprocessname), intentional mutable-accessor functions paired with an already-const twin (ipstack.c's storage_port/storage_port6/storage_sin_addr/storage_sin_addr6, and privsep.c's caller that exercises exactly that mutability), fixed external callback signatures (tls.c's OpenSSL session_ticket_cb, ftpd.c's SimpleConfSpecialHandler table entry), and standard-library calls whose own prototypes require a non-const pointer (fakechroot.c's stat()/lstat(), pure-pw.c's fprintf()). One FP (alt_arc4random.c's CHACHA20_ROUNDS) is a checker-side detection gap worth its own follow-up: the macro-expanded compound-assignment writes on its substituted array-index arguments aren't traced by the tool's write-analysis.
